@servers.sheet.usernamePlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the sign-in sheet's username field, shown when the server gave no hint about who signs in. "barry" is a sample first name; swap it for a typical sample name in the target language if appropriate. The word before it is the ordinary label your language puts in front of an example.

servers.pinHint.title: Your Network group is getting long

@servers.pinHint.title.description: Title of a one-time notification, shown the first time five servers sit in the volume switcher's Network group. "Network group" is the heading in the switcher (the dropdown listing disks and servers) that servers are filed under; use the same wording as that heading. Friendly and factual, never a warning.

servers.pinHint.body: Right-click a server and choose Unpin, or use "{command}" from the command palette. It stays in the Servers list.

@servers.pinHint.body.description: Body of that notification: how to take a server out of the volume switcher, and the reassurance that unpinning loses nothing. "Unpin" must match the context-menu item menu.network.unpin word for word. "Servers" is the hub row in the switcher that lists every saved server. The command name arrives translated in {command}; keep the quotation marks your language uses around a UI label.

placeholders.command: the name of the command palette entry that pins or unpins a server, already translated

@servers.pinHint.favorites.description: One extra line in that notification, added only when the user also has three or more favorites: favorites can be taken out of the switcher the same way servers can. "Favorites" is the switcher group holding folders the user saved.

@servers.pinHint.gotIt.description: VERB phrase (imperative), the button that dismisses the notification. Casual acknowledgement, the way a person says "understood" and moves on. Two or three words at most.

@servers.hub.colName.description: Column heading in the servers hub: the server''s own name. One or two words; the column is narrow.

@servers.hub.colType.description: Column heading in the servers hub for which protocol a server speaks (SFTP, WebDAV, SMB). One word.

@servers.hub.colAddress.description: Column heading in the servers hub for where the server lives: a hostname, an IP address, or a web address. One word.

@servers.hub.colStatus.description: Column heading in the servers hub for how the server is doing right now. One word.

@servers.hub.colLastUsed.description: Column heading in the servers hub for when the user last connected to the server. Two words at most.

@servers.hub.addServer.description: The last row of the servers hub, which opens the form for typing a new server. VERB phrase, imperative. The ellipsis is the single character … (U+2026) and means "this opens something"; keep it.

@servers.hub.status.connected.description: Status of a server the app is talking to right now. One word, ADJECTIVE.

@servers.hub.status.saved.description: Status of a server the user has saved but isn''t connected to. Nothing is wrong; it''s simply idle. One word, ADJECTIVE.

@servers.hub.status.foundNearby.description: Status of a server Cmdr can see on the local network right now, whether or not the user saved it. Two words.

@servers.hub.status.signedOut.description: Status of a saved server whose session ended because a password is what''s missing. ❗ NOT a rejection and not a fault: the user simply has to sign in again.

servers.hub.status.waitingForKey: Waiting for you to check the key

@servers.hub.status.waitingForKey.description: Status of an SSH server whose identity key the user hasn''t approved yet. "The key" is the server''s SSH host key, a fingerprint a person compares before trusting the server. Address the user directly.

@servers.hub.neverUsed.description: Shown in the servers hub''s "Last used" column for a server the user has never connected to. One word.

@servers.hub.discoveryOff.description: One line in the servers hub, in place of the list of servers found nearby, when the user has turned local network discovery off in Settings. Saved servers still work and are still listed; this line is only about the nearby ones.

@servers.hub.discoveryOffLink.description: Link beside the discovery-off line; it opens Settings at the switch that turns local network discovery back on. VERB phrase, imperative. "Settings" is the app''s own Settings window; use the word your language''s macOS uses for it.

@servers.hub.emptyTitle.description: Heading of the empty state in the servers hub, when the user has saved none and Cmdr found none nearby. Short and neutral.

servers.hub.emptyMessage: Add one below, or turn on a Mac or NAS on your network and Cmdr will find it.

@servers.hub.emptyMessage.description: One line under the empty-state heading in the servers hub. "NAS" is a network storage box; keep the abbreviation if your language uses it, otherwise say the equivalent. "below" points at the "Add server…" row at the bottom of the list.

@servers.hub.rowCount.description: The count in the status bar under the servers hub. Counts saved servers and nearby ones together, and excludes the "Add server…" row.

placeholders.count: the number, for choosing the plural form
placeholders.countText: the number as the user''s locale writes it, like "1,024"

@servers.paneState.connecting.description: Heading of the pane view shown while Cmdr opens a connection to a server. {name} is the server''s display name. The ellipsis is the single character … (U+2026).
@servers.paneState.connecting.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

servers.paneState.connectingHint: This can take a few seconds.

@servers.paneState.connectingHint.description: One line under the connecting heading, setting the expectation that a server handshake is not instant. Reassurance, not an instruction.
@servers.paneState.connectingHint.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.paneState.cancel.description: Button that calls off a connection Cmdr is in the middle of opening. VERB, imperative.
@servers.paneState.cancel.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.paneState.tryAgain.description: Button that starts the same connection over after it was refused. VERB phrase, imperative.
@servers.paneState.tryAgain.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.paneState.disconnect.description: Button that drops the server''s session and leaves the pane. VERB, imperative. A server has nothing to unplug, so it says Disconnect rather than Eject.
@servers.paneState.disconnect.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.refusal.authenticationRejected.description: Shown in the pane when the server refused the credential Cmdr offered. Factual, not accusing: the password may have changed on the server side.

placeholders.username: the account name on the server, like "ada"

servers.refusal.needsCredentials: This server asks for a password.

@servers.refusal.needsCredentials.description: Shown in the pane when the server wants a credential and Cmdr has none stored. ❗ NOT a rejection: nothing was ever offered, so don''t word it as a wrong password.

servers.refusal.accountNotPermitted: {username} doesn''t have access here. Try a different account.

@servers.refusal.accountNotPermitted.description: Shown in the sign-in sheet when the server accepted the account, but the place being opened (for example a network share) doesn''t let that account in. ❗ NOT a wrong password: the sign-in worked, so don''t word it as a rejected credential. "Here" is the place named in the sheet''s header.

placeholders.username: the account name on the server, like "ada"

servers.refusal.authMethodUnsupported: This server uses a sign-in method Cmdr doesn''t support yet.

@servers.refusal.authMethodUnsupported.description: Shown in the pane when the server challenged with an authentication scheme Cmdr doesn''t speak. The secret was never sent, so nothing about it is known to be wrong. ❌ Don''t name the scheme: it means nothing to the reader.

servers.refusal.certificateUntrusted: macOS doesn''t trust this server''s certificate. Add it in Keychain Access, then try again.

@servers.refusal.certificateUntrusted.description: Shown in the pane when a WebDAV server''s TLS certificate isn''t trusted by the operating system. "Keychain Access" is the macOS app name, which the OS ships translated; use the name your language''s macOS uses.

servers.refusal.notAWebdavServer: Nothing at this address answers WebDAV.

@servers.refusal.notAWebdavServer.description: Shown in the pane when the address answers as a web server but doesn''t speak WebDAV. "WebDAV" is a protocol name; don''t translate it.

servers.refusal.invalidUrl: That doesn''t look like a server address.

@servers.refusal.invalidUrl.description: Shown in the pane when the saved address isn''t a usable web address at all.

@servers.refusal.timedOut.description: Shown in the pane when the server didn''t finish the handshake inside Cmdr''s budget.

placeholders.host: the server''s hostname or address, like "nas.local"

@servers.refusal.unreachable.description: Shown in the pane when there was no route to the server at all: it''s off, the name doesn''t resolve, or the network is down. "Cmdr" is the product name.

placeholders.host: the server''s hostname or address, like "nas.local"

@servers.refusal.hostKeyUntrusted.description: Shown in the pane when an SSH server presents a host key this Mac hasn''t approved. "Key" is the server''s SSH host key, the fingerprint a person checks before trusting the server.

placeholders.host: the server''s hostname or address, like "nas.local"

servers.refusal.hostKeyRevoked: {host}''s key is marked as compromised in your SSH settings on this Mac. Cmdr won''t connect to it.

@servers.refusal.hostKeyRevoked.description: Shown in the pane when the server''s SSH host key is listed as revoked in the user''s own known_hosts file. This one is deliberately final: there is no button that can safely undo it. "SSH" is a protocol name; don''t translate it.

placeholders.host: the server''s hostname or address, like "nas.local"

servers.refusal.startFolderOutsideRoot: The start folder has to be the root folder or a folder inside it.

@servers.refusal.startFolderOutsideRoot.description: Shown under the Start folder field of the add or edit server sheet when the typed start folder is neither the root folder nor a folder inside it. Nothing was saved or dialed. Calm and instructive. "Start folder" and "root folder" must use the same words as the field labels (servers.sheet.startFolder and servers.sheet.rootFolder).

servers.refusal.rootNotFound: Cmdr can''t open this folder on {host}. Check that it exists and that your account can read it.

@servers.refusal.rootNotFound.description: Shown under the Root folder field when the user saves an edit to a server that is connected right now, and the server has no folder at that path this account can open: it is missing, it is a file, or access is refused. Nothing was saved. "Cmdr" is the product name.

placeholders.host: the server''s hostname or address, like "nas.local"

servers.refusal.startFolderNotFound: Cmdr can''t open this start folder on {host}. Check that it exists and that your account can read it.

@servers.refusal.startFolderNotFound.description: Shown under the Start folder field when the user saves an edit to a server that is connected right now, and the server has no folder at the start folder path this account can open: it is missing, it is a file, or access is refused. Nothing was saved. "start folder" must match the servers.sheet.startFolder label. "Cmdr" is the product name.

placeholders.host: the server''s hostname or address, like "nas.local"

servers.refusal.saveUnconfirmed: {host} didn''t answer in time, so nothing was saved. Try again in a moment.

@servers.refusal.saveUnconfirmed.description: Shown above the buttons of the edit server sheet when saving needed the connected server to confirm a folder and it did not answer within a few seconds. Nothing was saved, and trying again is safe.

placeholders.host: the server''s hostname or address, like "nas.local"

@servers.sheet.addTitle.description: Title of the sheet where the user types a new server. VERB phrase, imperative.

@servers.sheet.signInTitle.description: Title of the sheet when a server is asking for a credential. VERB phrase, imperative.

@servers.sheet.editTitle.description: Title of the sheet when the user is changing a server they already saved. VERB phrase, imperative.

@servers.sheet.connect.description: The sheet's main button in add mode: it dials the server the user typed. VERB, imperative.

@servers.sheet.signIn.description: The sheet's main button when a server is asking for a credential. VERB phrase, imperative.

@servers.sheet.save.description: The sheet's main button when the user is editing a saved server. VERB, imperative.

@servers.sheet.cancel.description: The sheet's secondary button: it closes without connecting or saving. VERB, imperative.

@servers.sheet.connecting.description: Replaces the main button's label while the sheet is waiting for the server. The ellipsis is the single character … (U+2026).

@servers.sheet.protocolLegend.description: Accessible name of the SMB / SFTP / WebDAV picker in the add form. Screen readers only; not visible. One word, NOUN.

@servers.sheet.protocolSmb.description: One option of the protocol picker. A protocol name; keep it as-is.

@servers.sheet.protocolSftp.description: One option of the protocol picker. A protocol name; keep it as-is.

@servers.sheet.protocolWebdav.description: One option of the protocol picker. A protocol name; keep it as-is.

@servers.sheet.address.description: Label of the field where the user types where the server lives. One word, NOUN.

@servers.sheet.addressPlaceholder.description: Placeholder inside the address field. A short example hostname; leave it as-is or use an equally short one.

servers.sheet.addressHelp: A hostname, an address you copied, or a whole ssh line. Cmdr picks the protocol.

@servers.sheet.addressHelp.description: One line under the address field, telling the user they can paste whatever they have. “Cmdr” is the product name; “ssh” is a command name, keep it lowercase and untranslated.

servers.sheet.identityLocked: The address and the account are what name this server. Forget this server and add it again to change them.

@servers.sheet.identityLocked.description: Two lines under the greyed-out address and username fields when the user is EDITING a saved server, explaining why those two can't be typed in and what to do instead. “Forget” is the exact word on the menu item and palette command that removes a saved server, so use the same word your translation uses there.

@servers.sheet.username.description: Label of the account field. One word, NOUN.

@servers.sheet.password.description: Label of the password field. One word, NOUN.

@servers.sheet.passphrase.description: Label of the field for the passphrase that unlocks an SSH key FILE, which is not the account's password. Two words.

@servers.sheet.remember.description: Checkbox that stores the password in the macOS Keychain. “Keychain” is the macOS feature name, which the OS ships translated; use the name your language's macOS uses.

@servers.sheet.connectionModeLegend.description: Accessible name of the guest-or-account choice for a share that allows both. Screen readers only; not visible.

@servers.sheet.connectAsGuest.description: One option: open the share without an account, which some servers allow. VERB phrase, imperative.

servers.sheet.signInWithCredentials: Sign in with a username and password

@servers.sheet.signInWithCredentials.description: The other option: open the share as a named account. VERB phrase, imperative.

@servers.sheet.advanced.description: A collapsed section holding the settings most people never change. One word, ADJECTIVE.

servers.sheet.name: Name

@servers.sheet.name.description: Label of the field for what to call this server in the app. One word, NOUN.

servers.sheet.nameHelp: Leave it empty to call this server by its account and host.

@servers.sheet.nameHelp.description: One line under the Name field in the add and edit server sheets. An empty name makes Cmdr call the server by its account name and host, like ada@nas.local.

@servers.sheet.rootFolder.description: Label of the field for the folder ON THE SERVER this saved server is limited to: Cmdr never shows anything above it. Two words, NOUN phrase. The refusal messages and the start folder help reuse this term, so keep it consistent.

servers.sheet.rootFolderHelp: Cmdr never goes above this folder on the server.

@servers.sheet.rootFolderHelp.description: One line under the Root folder field, explaining that the folder is a ceiling: Cmdr never navigates above it on the server. "Cmdr" is the product name.

@servers.sheet.startFolder.description: Label of the field for the folder a pane opens at when the user opens this server. It must be the root folder or a folder inside it. Two words, NOUN phrase.

servers.sheet.startFolderHelp: Where the server opens. Leave it empty to open the root folder.

@servers.sheet.startFolderHelp.description: One line under the Start folder field: it is where the server opens, and leaving it empty opens the root folder. "root folder" must use the same words as the servers.sheet.rootFolder label.

@servers.sheet.keyFile.description: Label of the field for the SSH private key file to sign in with. “Key” is an SSH key. Two words.

@servers.sheet.browse.description: Button beside the key-file field; it opens the system file picker. VERB, imperative. The ellipsis is the single character … (U+2026) and means “this opens something”; keep it.

@servers.sheet.useAgent.description: Checkbox letting Cmdr ask the running ssh-agent for a key. “ssh-agent” is a program name; keep it as-is.

@servers.sheet.autoReconnect.description: Checkbox letting Cmdr redial this server on its own when the connection drops. VERB phrase, imperative.

servers.sheet.needsStoredSecret: Reconnecting on its own needs a remembered password. Turn on “Remember in Keychain” and sign in once.

@servers.sheet.needsStoredSecret.description: Shown in the edit sheet when “Reconnect automatically” is on but nothing is stored, so it can never actually run. Says what to do about it.

@servers.sheet.tryNextcloudAddress.description: Button offered when a web address answers but doesn't speak WebDAV. It appends the path Nextcloud and ownCloud keep their files under. “Nextcloud” is a product name; keep it as-is. VERB phrase, imperative.

@servers.hostKey.firstContactTitle.description: Heading of the step where the user approves a server's SSH identity key the first time. Routine, not alarming.

placeholders.host: the server''s hostname or address, like “nas.local”

servers.hostKey.firstContactBody: Check the fingerprint below against the one the server''s owner gave you, then trust it.

@servers.hostKey.firstContactBody.description: One line under that heading. “Fingerprint” is the short string that identifies an SSH key; a person compares it character by character.

@servers.hostKey.changedTitle.description: Heading of the same step when the server presents a DIFFERENT key than the one already trusted. This one is serious: it can mean someone is in the middle.

placeholders.host: the server''s hostname or address, like “nas.local”

servers.hostKey.changedBody: This can mean the server was reinstalled, or that something is sitting between you and it. Check the fingerprint with the server''s owner before trusting it.

@servers.hostKey.changedBody.description: One line under the changed-key heading. Says both innocent and serious causes, and what to do first.

@servers.hostKey.changedDisclosure.description: A collapsed section holding the button that trusts a CHANGED key. Deliberately behind a click, so trusting one is never a reflex. First person: the user speaking.

@servers.hostKey.fingerprintLabel.description: Label above the SSH key's algorithm and fingerprint. Two words, NOUN phrase.

@servers.hostKey.trustAndConnect.description: Button that records a first-contact key and carries on connecting. VERB phrase, imperative.

@servers.hostKey.trustNewKey.description: Button that records a CHANGED key, behind the disclosure. VERB phrase, imperative.

@servers.paneState.signedOut.description: Heading of the pane view shown when a server's session ended because a password is what's missing. ❗ NOT a rejection and not a fault: the user simply has to sign in again.
@servers.paneState.signedOut.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.paneState.signIn.description: Button that opens the form for signing in to the server again. VERB phrase, imperative. The ellipsis is the single character … (U+2026) and means “this opens something”; keep it.
@servers.paneState.signIn.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.paneState.hostKeyChanged.description: Heading of the pane view shown when an SSH server presents a different identity key than the one this Mac trusts. Serious: it can mean someone is in the middle. “Cmdr” is the product name.
@servers.paneState.hostKeyChanged.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

servers.paneState.hostKeyChangedHint: Its key changed. That can mean the server was reinstalled, or that something is sitting between you and it. Disconnect, then open it again to check the fingerprint.

@servers.paneState.hostKeyChangedHint.description: One line under that heading, saying both innocent and serious causes and what to do. “Key” is the server''s SSH host key; “fingerprint” is the short string a person compares before trusting it.
@servers.paneState.hostKeyChangedHint.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.paneState.reconnecting.description: Heading of the pane view shown while Cmdr keeps trying to bring back a server connection that dropped. ❗ NOT a first connection: the session existed and Cmdr is getting it back on its own. {name} is the server''s display name. The ellipsis is the single character … (U+2026).
@servers.paneState.reconnecting.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

servers.paneState.signedOutNothingToAsk: This server signs in with a key rather than a password, so there''s nothing to type. Open it again to retry.

@servers.paneState.signedOutNothingToAsk.description: One line under the "Signed out" heading, shown instead of a Sign in button when the server proves itself with an SSH key or an agent identity rather than a password. Say plainly that there is nothing for the user to enter and what they can do instead. ❗ Not an apology and not a fault.
@servers.paneState.signedOutNothingToAsk.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.paneState.retryProgressAriaLabe.description: Accessibility label for the countdown progress bar showing how long until the next reconnect attempt.
@servers.paneState.retryProgressAriaLabe.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.paneState.retryNow.description: Button that triggers a reconnect attempt immediately.
@servers.paneState.retryNow.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.paneState.retryNowTooltip.description: Hover tooltip for the button that triggers a reconnect attempt right away instead of waiting.
@servers.paneState.retryNowTooltip.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

servers.paneState.cancelCycleTooltip: Stop trying for now. The connection stays available. Switch back to retry.

@servers.paneState.cancelCycleTooltip.description: Hover tooltip for the button that pauses auto-reconnect while keeping the connection available to resume.
@servers.paneState.cancelCycleTooltip.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

servers.paneState.disconnectCycleTooltip: Stop trying and disconnect from the server.

@servers.paneState.disconnectCycleToolti.description: Hover tooltip for the button that stops reconnecting and drops the server connection.
@servers.paneState.disconnectCycleToolti.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

servers.paneState.retryKeepsTrying: Will keep trying for a total of {duration}.

@servers.paneState.retryKeepsTrying.description: Reassurance line telling the user how long the auto-reconnect will keep trying. {duration} is a phrase like "60 seconds" or "2 minutes".

placeholders.duration: the total duration phrase, e.g. 60 seconds or 2 minutes

@servers.paneState.retryKeepsTrying.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.paneState.retryTotalSeconds.description: Total reconnect-cycle duration phrased in seconds, embedded in the "Will keep trying for a total of …" sentence.

placeholders.seconds: the number of seconds, for choosing the plural form
placeholders.secondsText: the same number as the user's locale writes it, like "1,024"

@servers.paneState.retryTotalSeconds.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.paneState.retryTotalMinutes.description: Total reconnect-cycle duration phrased in minutes, embedded in the "Will keep trying for a total of …" sentence.

placeholders.minutes: the number of minutes, for choosing the plural form
placeholders.minutesText: the same number as the user's locale writes it, like "1,024"

@servers.paneState.retryTotalMinutes.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.
